trapping.note: a two-sided bound: adiabatic recovery can lower the photon share by at most about 3.3x; Comptonization (y about 133) pushes the other way. The sign is unresolved without radiation-hydrodynamic transport.

nonequilibrium.rule: Ti/Te is set by the balance of exchange (n^2) against heating (n^2): density cancels except in ln Lambda, so the sustained cases hold at any density; only finite confinement (n tau_E) adds loss, and n tau_ei ~ n tau_E means the two-temperature state is marginal wherever the burn is confined long enough to burn

verdict.next: radiation-hydrodynamic transport of the dense target (Compton trapping and Comptonization) is the single calculation that could move the source by more than a factor of a few; it cannot close the interface gap, which needs a nozzle closure 4-6 orders tighter than any computed or measured

answers.question: Photon radiation under the best defensible models
answers.answer: 10.1% of fusion power (S1, nominal); optimistic bound 8.3% (S1). 1.6's 16.4 % floor was 1.31x too high (electron count); the corrected same-lever floor is 12.6%. Compton trapping could lower the dense target by at most 3.3x (unresolved sign).

answers.question: How much may strike the ship
answers.answer: With every other load at zero, the drive share (10.8 GW, 2.7 GW per engine) allows 2.7 GW per engine at hot structure; at the mission point that is 5.2e-05 of the charged stream, Neutrons alone already put 424x the drive share into the hardware in the best case, so no photon share fits; with neutrons, leakage and losses all at zero, photons could be at most 6.6e-04 of fusion power (SR-1, mission point, cold parts shaded).

answers.question: Tolerable charged leakage
answers.answer: hot structure 5.2e-05, armour 2.3e-05, warm machinery 4.6e-06, cryogenic 1.8e-07 of the charged power (mission point); Engine 1.4 computed 18.3% at best.

answers.question: Can polarization and non-equilibrium close the gap
answers.answer: No. Polarization gives at most 1.5x fusion at the same electron heating; hot-ion and prompt-escape states trade photons for auxiliary heating (Rider); together they move the photon share by a factor of a few against a gap of orders of magnitude.

answers.question: What limits directed exhaust energy
answers.answer: Photons (10-60 % of fusion) and capture: Engine 1.4's best closure sends 82 % of the charged energy aft; the canon 0.8 directed efficiency needs photons + neutrons + leakage below 20 % together.

answers.question: Are the coils survivable
answers.answer: Fluence limits, removal lengths and shield density are the 1.6A brackets (nominal used); no asserted conductor lifetime, no nanomaterial immunity. Shield heat lands at 700 K and is lifted to the radiator. S0-SC: shield 45,422 t vs margin 174 t, FAIL; S1: shield 42,692 t vs margin 174 t, FAIL

answers.question: What closes the radiator budget
answers.answer: Nothing defensible. The feasibility map's best mission closure needs photons 1e-01, deposition 1e-03, leakage 1e-04 (UNSUPPORTED)

answers.question: Fundamental constraints vs engineering challenges
answers.answer: Fundamental: bremsstrahlung of a D-3He burn hot enough to burn (tens of percent), the magnet sky, D-D neutrons. Engineering: leakage, shielding mass, cold-part shading, power conversion.

answers.question: Is the four-engine architecture worth developing
answers.answer: As a representation, yes (it is canon and unchanged); as a radiation and thermal design, not with this source: the gap is in the source and the interface, not in the number of engines.
